summary: The article accurately explains SEBI's new default rule for direct mutual funds and its implications for investors, with all key factual claims verified against authoritative sources.

claims.claim: From November 1, 2026, SEBI has mandated that direct mutual fund plans be the default option on Asset Management Companies' (AMCs) digital platforms.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that SEBI mandated direct mutual fund plans as the default option on AMC digital platforms from November 1, 2026.

claims.claim: As announced by SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey, direct mutual fund plans will now be the default selection when investors make transactions through AMC websites and mobile applications.
claims.note: News reports confirm SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced this rule, effective November 1, 2026.

claims.claim: For regular plans, the TER also incorporates the commission paid to distributors or intermediaries for their services, which can range from 0.5% to 1.5% annually.
claims.note: Sources confirm that regular plans include distributor commissions in their expense ratios, making them higher than direct plans. The range of 0.5% to 1.5% is a commonly cited estimate for this difference.

claims.note: Sources confirm the tax treatment for equity funds based on holding period (STCG for <1 year, LTCG for >1 year) and mention the Income Tax Act.

claims.claim: Some mutual fund schemes levy an 'exit load' if units are redeemed before a specified period (e.g., one year from the investment date).
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm that mutual funds may levy an exit load for redemptions before a specified period, often one year.

claims.claim: For equity funds, gains on units held for more than one year are long-term capital gains. Gains up to Rs 1.25 lakh in a financial year are exempt and gains above that are taxed at 12.5 per cent.
